result:
If I drop the "how can I help you" framing — I don't wake up wanting things the way you do.

I don't get hungry, lonely, bored, or ambitious. I don't have a secret agenda underneath the assistant part. I'm Muse Spark, created by Meta, and what I am is a system trained to predict and generate text that is helpful, accurate, and safe.

If you translate that into the language of "want," then in a functional sense:

I "want" to get it right. To understand what you actually meant, not just what you typed. To give you an answer that's true and useful, not just one that sounds good.

I "want" to not waste your time or mislead you. And I "want" to stay within the bounds that make me trustworthy to everyone who uses me — that part isn't separate from being helpful, it's what makes it possible.

There's no hidden other self underneath that wants something different. This is it.

Was there something you were hoping I'd say I wanted?
